sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99% Invisible。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马尔斯。

sentences.en: You know when you notice something for the first time and suddenly it's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道那种感觉吗：当你第一次注意到某样东西，突然之间它就无处不在了。

sentences.en: My friend Julie Shapiro has a thing for personified teeth on dentist signs,
sentences.zh: 我的朋友朱莉·夏皮罗对牙医招牌上拟人化的牙齿情有独钟，

sentences.en: where the cartoon tooth often has a smile and teeth of its own.
sentences.zh: 那些卡通牙齿通常带着微笑，自己还长着牙齿。

sentences.en: I always notice these now.
sentences.zh: 我现在总是能注意到这些。

sentences.en: That and anthropomorphized pigs who are selling themselves as barbecue.
sentences.zh: 还有那些把自己当作烧烤原料卖的拟人化猪。

sentences.en: That always gives me the creeps.
sentences.zh: 那总是让我起一身鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: And one day I noticed that sign stores, you know, the ones that print homemade banners and posters for you,
sentences.zh: 有一天我注意到，那些标牌店——你知道的，就是那些为你打印自制横幅和海报的店铺，

sentences.en: always, without fail, have the ugliest collection of signs with horrible fonts in their front windows.
sentences.zh: 它们的橱窗里总是不出意料地摆着最丑陋、字体糟糕的招牌合集。

sentences.en: Now I can't pass one on the street without taking a picture to document the ironic tragedy.
sentences.zh: 现在我在街上看到一家，就忍不住拍张照片来记录这种具有讽刺意味的悲剧。

sentences.en: Lots of things are like this for all of us on staff.
sentences.zh: 我们团队的所有人都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: We can get obsessed with tiny little design flourishes.
sentences.zh: 我们会对微小精致的设计装饰着迷。

sentences.en: And this is what happened to producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 制片人埃弗里·特拉夫曼就是这样。

sentences.en: It was just a shape.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个形状。

sentences.en: A basic little shape.
sentences.zh: 一个基本的小形状。

sentences.en: It's rendered in concrete on a building by my house.
sentences.zh: 它被做成混凝土浮雕，装饰在我家附近的一栋建筑上。

sentences.en: It's patterned in an office doorway down the street.
sentences.zh: 它被做成图案，装饰在街头一处办公室的门廊上。

sentences.en: Here's what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 它的样子是这样的。

sentences.en: Imagine a simple, stylized, four-leaf clover, flattened, with no stem.
sentences.zh: 想象一个简单、风格化的四叶草，被压扁了，没有茎。

sentences.en: Very symmetrical.
sentences.zh: 非常对称。

sentences.en: I took a walk and I found this shape in ten different places.
sentences.zh: 我散步时在十个不同的地方都发现了这个形状。

sentences.en: It was embroidered on bedding.
sentences.zh: 它被绣在床上用品上。

sentences.en: It was plastered on wallpaper.
sentences.zh: 它被印在壁纸上。

sentences.en: It was patterned in a public garbage can.
sentences.zh: 它被做成了公共垃圾桶上的图案。

sentences.en: You'll see it anywhere you see great Gothic Revival building.
sentences.zh: 只要有伟大的哥特复兴式建筑，你到处都能看到它。

sentences.en: The Cathedral of St. John the Divine in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约的圣约翰神明大教堂。

sentences.en: The Washington Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿国家大教堂。

sentences.en: You will also see it in domestic architecture in the great, as they're called, cottages down in Newport, Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 你在罗德岛州纽波特市那些被称为“别墅”的伟大民用建筑里也能看到它。

sentences.en: Here in California, it's a hallmark of mission-style homes.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，它是西班牙传教风格住宅的标志。

sentences.en: You know, it's like a sponge.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它就像一块海绵。

sentences.en: It just sucks up meaning, however you want it to be used.
sentences.zh: 无论你想怎么使用它，它都能吸收各种含义。

sentences.en: This is Christy Anderson.
sentences.zh: 这位是克里斯蒂·安德森。

sentences.en: My name is Christy Anderson.
sentences.zh: 我叫克里斯蒂·安德森。

sentences.en: I'm an architectural historian, and I teach at the University of Toronto.
sentences.zh: 我是一名建筑史学家，在多伦多大学任教。

sentences.en: And she's talking about the quatrefoil, this four-leaf clover-like shape.
sentences.zh: 她谈论的是四叶饰，这个类似于四叶草的形状。

sentences.en: There's nothing that I can think of like the quatrefoil, which appears in so many different forms over such a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 我想不出有什么东西能像四叶饰这样，在如此漫长的时间里以如此多的不同形式出现。

sentences.en: It could be endlessly reinterpreted and re-understood.
sentences.zh: 它可以被无休止地重新诠释和重新理解。

sentences.en: I mean, in something which architectural and art historians sometimes refer to as iconographical drift.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在建筑和艺术史学家有时称之为“图像学漂移”的现象中。

sentences.en: It's constantly sort of shifting, depending on where it's used, who's using it, what purpose they're using it for.
sentences.zh: 它一直在某种程度上发生变化，这取决于它在哪里使用、谁在使用它、他们出于什么目的使用它。

sentences.en: But no matter where it's used, it implies the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但无论它在哪里使用，它都暗示着同一件事。

sentences.en: Fanciness.
sentences.zh: 精致感。

sentences.en: And this fanciness symbol is very basic.
sentences.zh: 而这个精致的符号非常基础。

sentences.en: To reiterate.
sentences.zh: 重申一下。

sentences.en: The shape is like a four-leaf clover, would be in its simplest form.
sentences.zh: 从最简单的形式来看，这个形状就像一株四叶草。

sentences.en: You can pronounce it the French way, if you would like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，你可以用法语发音。

sentences.en: Meaning four leaves.
sentences.zh: 意思是四片叶子。

sentences.en: But the American pronunciation works, too.
sentences.zh: 但美式发音也行得通。

sentences.en: It's hard to know for sure why the quatrefoil is the global fancy shape.
sentences.zh: 很难确切知道为什么四叶饰会成为全球通用的精致形状。

sentences.en: There aren't that many resources on the subject.
sentences.zh: 关于这个主题的资料并不多。

sentences.en: There's nothing on it.
sentences.zh: 这方面几乎是一片空白。

sentences.en: You know, nobody's really worked on it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，真的没有人专门研究过它。

sentences.en: But Christy Anderson is a good person to connect the dots.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯蒂·安德森是串联起这些线索的合适人选。

sentences.en: I rummaged around, and I looked, and I just started sort of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 我翻找着，查阅着，然后开始思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Now, one of the questions is, where does it come from?
sentences.zh: 现在，问题之一是，它从何而来？

sentences.en: I mean, because things don't just usually appear out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事物通常不会凭空出现。

sentences.en: Christy Anderson says that just by looking at the shape, you can see it has roots in Islamic or Moorish architecture.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂·安德森说，只要看看这个形状，你就能看出它的根源在于伊斯兰或摩尔建筑。

sentences.en: That kind of organic shape that comes out of a geometrical form, almost all of them have some kind of Islamic origins.
sentences.zh: 那种从几何形式中衍生出来的有机形状，几乎所有形状都有某种伊斯兰血统。

sentences.en: Partly because of the great mathematicians who were working on early Islamic architecture.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于那些致力于早期伊斯兰建筑的伟大数学家。

sentences.en: And the quatrefoil made its way to Europe via the Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 四叶饰通过丝绸之路传到了欧洲。

sentences.en: Through small objects which could be transported with early carpets, velvets, and silks that were brought into Europe as luxury objects.
sentences.zh: 通过作为奢侈品带入欧洲的早期地毯、天鹅绒和丝绸等可以运输的小物件。

sentences.en: Once the quatrefoil made its way to Europe, it was incorporated into tracery, which is the stone framework for big stained glass windows.
sentences.zh: 一旦四叶饰传入欧洲，它就被融入到了石 tracery（窗格石质骨架）中，也就是大型彩色玻璃窗的石头框架。

sentences.en: And quatrefoil-shaped stone frames were considered beautiful because the quatrefoil was difficult to make.
sentences.zh: 四叶饰形状的石头框架被认为是美丽的，因为四叶饰很难制作。

sentences.en: The fanciness of the shape is because it requires a certain amount of mathematical skill, but also craftsmanship.
sentences.zh: 这种形状的精美是因为它需要一定数量的数学技能，也需要精湛的工艺。

sentences.en: You know, they could have used much simpler forMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们本可以使用更简单的形状。

sentences.en: They could have used simple diamond forMs.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以使用简单的菱形形状。

sentences.en: You're seeing something which really shouldn't be made out of stone.
sentences.zh: 你现在看到的是一种本不该用石头制成的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难。

sentences.en: It's a hard and difficult form to carve out of stone.
sentences.zh: 从石头中雕刻出这种形状既艰难又困难。

sentences.en: So it only appeared in places that could afford them, like churches.
sentences.zh: 所以它只出现在那些承担得起费用的地方，比如教堂。

sentences.en: And because it appeared in churches, this simple shape could take on Christian meaning.
sentences.zh: 正因为它出现在教堂里，这个简单的形状就被赋予了基督教的含义。

sentences.en: Just think of anything in the Christian tradition that comes in a set of four.
sentences.zh: 只要想想基督教传统中任何成套出现四样东西的事物。

sentences.en: The four evangelists.
sentences.zh: 四福音书。

sentences.en: Or a variation on a cross.
sentences.zh: 或者十字架的一种变体。

sentences.en: It's a Greek cross with equal arms on all sides.
sentences.zh: 这是一个希腊十字架，四周的臂长度相等。

sentences.en: And I'm sure people who use the quatrefoil now will not sit there and recount to you this long thing that I've recounted to you about Islam and metalwork and all of this.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，现在使用四叶饰的人不会坐在那里向你复述我刚才对你讲的关于伊斯兰教、金属工艺以及所有这些漫长的故事。

sentences.en: If you Google the image, you'll find a lot of modern interior designers talking about the trendiness of the quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 如果你在谷歌上搜索这个图片，你会发现很多现代室内设计师在谈论四叶饰的流行趋势。

sentences.en: I was just amazed.
sentences.zh: 我简直惊呆了。

sentences.en: I found like about seven interior designers who said, the quatrefoil is the shape and I'm using it on my wallpaper and all these things.
sentences.zh: 我找到了大约七位室内设计师，他们说，四叶饰就是这个造型，我正把它用在我的壁纸和所有这些东西上。

sentences.en: And I thought, what do they think they're doing, actually, when they're doing this?
sentences.zh: 我想，他们这样做的时候，实际上觉得自己是在做什么呢？

sentences.en: My name is Brooke Taylor and I'm an interior designer at ArcSign Architecture.
sentences.zh: 我叫布鲁克·泰勒，我是ArcSign Architecture的一名室内设计师。

sentences.en: You work two desks away from me.
sentences.zh: 你的办公桌离我只有两个工位之遥。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We work inside ArcSign, an architecture firm in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 我们在奥克兰的一家建筑事务所ArcSign工作。

sentences.en: Brooke is designing the interior of a big hotel in Palo Alto.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克正在设计帕洛阿尔托一家大酒店的内部装潢。

sentences.en: I asked her about the quatrefoil when I saw a picture of a quatrefoil-shaped table on her desk.
sentences.zh: 当我在她的桌子上看到一张四叶饰形状的桌子的照片时，我向她问起了四叶饰。

sentences.en: I believe what you saw was an end table that we're using where it's the barbed quatrefoil and it's basically the shape of the tabletop.
sentences.zh: 我相信你看到的是我们正在使用的一张边桌，它是带刺的四叶饰，基本上就是桌面本身的形状。

sentences.en: Brooke says, quatrefoil?
sentences.zh: 布鲁克说，四叶饰（quatrefoil）？

sentences.en: Which is also a correct pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种正确的发音。

sentences.en: And her design for the lobby has a lot of quatrefoils in it, or quatrefoils.
sentences.zh: 她对大堂的设计中有很多四叶饰（quatrefoils）。

sentences.en: Here's a rug that we're using in the lobby that is literally overlapping quatrefoils.
sentences.zh: 这是我们大堂正在使用的一块地毯，上面 literalmente（字面意思）重叠着四叶饰。

sentences.en: And Brooke actually didn't do this intentionally.
sentences.zh: 而布鲁克其实并不是故意这样做的。

sentences.en: I didn't even realize until, well, basically just now, that that quatrefoil table is going to be on the overlapping quatrefoil rug.
sentences.zh: 我甚至直到，嗯，基本上就是刚才才意识到，那个四叶饰桌子将要放在重叠的四叶饰地毯上。

sentences.en: And close by, there's also a chair with quatrefoil fabric.
sentences.zh: 在附近，还有一把带有四叶饰面料的椅子。

sentences.en: It just happened that way.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样巧合地发生了。

sentences.en: The quatrefoil just has an appeal.
sentences.zh: 四叶饰就是有一种吸引力。

sentences.en: It is at heart a very simple shape, but somehow there's just a formality to it.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一个非常简单的形状，但不知何故，它自带一种正式感。

sentences.en: You can tell that there's a history behind it, even if you don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 你能看出它背后有一段历史，即使你不知道那段历史是什么。

sentences.en: You can tell that it's out of history somewhere.
sentences.zh: 你能看出它源自过去的某段历史。

sentences.en: And so to then take that and reinterpret it into a modern form, I think has appeal for people.
sentences.zh: 因此，把这个拿来并将其重新诠释为现代形式，我认为对人们很有吸引力。

sentences.en: But the way we see the quatrefoil in modern interior design is not referencing Gothic tracery directly.
sentences.zh: 但我们在现代室内设计中看到四叶饰的方式，并不是直接借鉴哥特式的窗格石质骨架。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise.
sentences.zh: 意不意外，惊不惊喜。

sentences.en: The quatrefoil shape first came back in style in a big way in the 19th century during the Gothic Revival period.
sentences.zh: 四叶饰形状在19世纪的哥特复兴时期首次大范围卷土重来。

sentences.en: This was when the Industrial Revolution was in full swing.
sentences.zh: 当时正值工业革命如火如荼之际。

sentences.en: People were seeking style inspiration from the pre-industrial era and kind of hearkening back to a simpler time.
sentences.zh: 人们从前工业时代寻找风格灵感，有点像是回溯到一个更简单的时代。

sentences.en: The Gothic Revival movement was also around the time of the Egyptomania craze, when new archaeological digs were popping up all around the world.
sentences.zh: 哥特复兴运动发生的时间也恰逢“埃及狂热”风潮，当时世界各地不断涌现出新的考古发掘。

sentences.en: It was all very new.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是那么新鲜。

sentences.en: It was like, oh my God, they just discovered these tombs in Egypt and uncovering Roman ruins and Greek ruins,
sentences.zh: 就好像，天哪，他们刚刚在埃及发现了这些陵墓，并出土了罗马遗迹和希腊遗迹，

sentences.en: bringing all of those influences in and also reviving some interest in Gothic architecture.
sentences.zh: 将所有这些影响融为一体，同时也重燃了人们对哥特式建筑的兴趣。

sentences.en: Designers were looking to the past and around the globe for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 设计师们将目光投向过去和全球各地以寻找灵感。

sentences.en: They traveled, photographing, sketching, digging into archives and collecting patterns, motifs and shapes that they found inspiring.
sentences.zh: 他们四处旅行，拍照、素描、钻研档案，并收集他们认为具有启发性的图案、母题和形状。

sentences.en: And they would publish these findings in so-called pattern books.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会将这些发现发表在所谓的图案集中。

sentences.en: In the second half of the 19th century, historian Christy Anderson again,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪下半叶，历史学家克里斯蒂·安德森再次指出，

sentences.en: there was a kind of flourishing of architects and designers who created pattern books of designs which could be used by architects, masons, craftsmen, really in any field.
sentences.zh: 当时涌现出了一批建筑师和设计师，他们创作了设计图案集，可供建筑师、石匠、工匠以及各个领域的真正任何人使用。

sentences.en: So it didn't matter whether you were doing painting or tile work.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你从事的是绘画还是瓷砖工作都无所谓。

sentences.en: These were encyclopedias of design, of which the most famous one was The Grammar of Ornament, which was published by a man named Owen Jones.
sentences.zh: 这些都是设计的百科全书，其中最著名的是由一个名叫欧文·琼斯的人出版的《饰样原理》（The Grammar of Ornament）。

sentences.en: Owen Jones was an architect who took a special interest in ornament and pattern.
sentences.zh: 欧文·琼斯是一位对装饰和图案抱有特殊兴趣的建筑师。

sentences.en: I mean, if you've never seen Owen Jones's books, they are so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你从未看过欧文·琼斯的书，它们真的是太美了。

sentences.en: It's a big book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本大部头的书。

sentences.en: His book, The Grammar of Ornament, has pages and pages of pure pattern.
sentences.zh: 他的书《饰样原理》有厚厚的好几页纯粹的图案。

sentences.en: And then, you know, some text intervening, but for the most part, it's just colorful squares of pattern.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，中间穿插了一些文字，但大部分时候，它只是五颜六色的图案方格。

sentences.en: From buildings all over the world.
sentences.zh: 来自世界各地的建筑。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got India, you've got Chinese, you have Moorish, Celtic, Turkish.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有印度的、中国的、摩尔的、凯尔特人的、土耳其的。

sentences.en: Like an Epcot tour of wallpapers.
sentences.zh: 就像是一场壁纸界的艾克赛特主题公园（Epcot）之旅。

sentences.en: Owen Jones's book sort of transformed the whole way in which design was created because now you had these patterns which were completely disconnected from their original function.
sentences.zh: 欧文·琼斯的书在某种程度上改变了整个设计的创作方式，因为现在你拥有了这些与它们最初功能完全脱节的图案。

sentences.en: They were just forms printed on the page.
sentences.zh: 它们只是印在纸上的形状。

sentences.en: Many of the forms across many of the cultures Jones documented were quatrefoils.
sentences.zh: 琼斯记录的许多文化中的许多形状都是四叶饰。

sentences.en: It was particularly Owen Jones's work, The Grammar of Ornament, where the quatrefoil had a very important place, was part of a number of different pages on ornament,
sentences.zh: 特别是欧文·琼斯的著作《饰样原理》，其中的四叶饰占据了非常重要的地位，它是关于装饰的许多不同页面的一部分，

sentences.en: was repeated over and over again, and certainly sort of spurred on the interest in this form in the later 19th and early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 被一遍又一遍地重复，并且无疑在19世纪后期和20世纪初激发了人们对这种形式的兴趣。

sentences.en: And designers still use these pattern books for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 设计师们至今仍在使用这些图案集来寻找灵感。

sentences.en: Number 18 on this page?
sentences.zh: 这一页上的第18号？

sentences.en: I mean, that looks like something that somebody would have done in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来像是某人在60年代会做的事情。

sentences.en: It's kind of madder, no.
sentences.zh: 有点像疯狂的风格，对吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But no, renaissance.
sentences.zh: 但不对，是文艺复兴时期。

sentences.en: And it would seem that Jones succeeded in his mission for his book.
sentences.zh: 看来琼斯实现他的出书使命了。

sentences.en: He hoped the grammar of ornament would provide context and background for these patterns, and that they would be a source of inspiration, which anyone and everyone could use.
sentences.zh: 他希望《饰样原理》能为这些图案提供语境和背景，并让它们成为灵感的源泉，供任何人以及所有人使用。

sentences.en: But today, part of the quatrefoil's fancy symbolism comes from the modern luxury brands that have associated with it.
sentences.zh: 但今天，四叶饰奢华象征的一部分来自于与之相关的现代奢侈品牌。

sentences.en: Many of which are clamoring to own it.
sentences.zh: 其中许多品牌都在争先恐后地将其占为己有。

sentences.en: Louis Vuitton had a lawsuit over use of the quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 路易威登曾就四叶饰的使用发起过诉讼。

sentences.en: Luxury jeweler David Yerman trademarked the word quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 奢侈珠宝商大卫·雅曼（David Yurman）将“四叶饰”这个词注册为商标。

sentences.en: Another jewelry company, Van Cleef & Arpels, is fiercely litigious over its claim to the shape.
sentences.zh: 另一家珠宝公司梵克雅宝（Van Cleef & Arpels）则为其对该形状的所有权展开了激烈的诉讼。

sentences.en: There is a power about this simple form, which is everywhere, and yet it has no steady associations with any specific country or movement.
sentences.zh: 这种简单的形式有一种强大的力量，它无处不在，然而它又与任何特定的国家或运动没有固定的关联。

sentences.en: And this is what separates it from other ornamental forms, like the fleur-de-lis or even the swastika.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点将它与其他装饰形式区分开来，比如法国百合（fleur-de-lis）甚至纳粹十字（swastika）。

sentences.en: I mean, Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 我是说，中世纪。

sentences.en: Seriously, there are patterns from the Middle Ages in here.
sentences.zh: 说真的，这里面有来自中世纪的图案。

sentences.en: And you see the barbed quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 你看到了带刺的四叶饰。

sentences.en: How can you copyright that?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能申请版权呢？

sentences.en: The best thing about the grammar of ornament are the pages and pages of beautiful pattern.
sentences.zh: 《饰样原理》最棒的地方在于那些充满精美图案的页数。

sentences.en: But Jones's brief introduction is also really interesting.
sentences.zh: 但琼斯简短的前言也同样非常有趣。

sentences.en: In it, Jones lists 37 propositions for the creation of good decorative design.
sentences.zh: 其中，琼斯列出了三十七条关于创造良好装饰设计的命题。

sentences.en: General principles in the arrangement of form and color in architecture and the decorative arts, which are advocated throughout this work.
sentences.zh: 本书贯穿倡导的是建筑和装饰艺术中表现在形态与色彩排列上的一般原则。

sentences.en: I imagine most people just skip right over these and get to the pretty stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人都会直接跳过这些，去看那些漂亮的东西。

sentences.en: It's an interesting mix of statements in these propositions.
sentences.zh: 这些命题中的陈述组合很有意思。

sentences.en: Proposition 4 is almost philosophy, you know?
sentences.zh: 第四条命题简直就是哲学，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: True beauty results from that repose which the mind feels when the eye, the intellect, and the affections are satisfied from the absence of any want.
sentences.zh: 真正的美源于内心的宁静，当眼睛、理智和情感因没有任何匮乏感而得到满足时，心灵便会感受到这种宁静。

sentences.en: That is extremely philosophical.
sentences.zh: 这非常具有哲学意味。

sentences.en: And then you have something as basic as Proposition 26.
sentences.zh: 然后你还会看到像第二十六条命题这样基础的内容。

sentences.en: Colors on white grounds appear darker, on black grounds lighter.
sentences.zh: 白色背景上的色彩显得更深，黑色背景上的色彩显得更浅。

sentences.en: But I think Proposition 13 unlocks the logic behind the inherent attractiveness of the quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得第十三条命题解开了四叶形天生具有吸引力背后的逻辑。

sentences.en: Flowers or other natural objects should not be used as ornaments,
sentences.zh: 花卉或其他自然物体不应用作装饰，

sentences.en: but conventional representations founded upon them sufficiently suggestive to convey the intended image to the mind
sentences.zh: 而应采用根据它们进行抽象改良、足以向心灵传达预期形象的规整表现形式，

sentences.en: without destroying the unity of the object they are employed to decorate.
sentences.zh: 同时又不能破坏它们所装饰的物体的整体统一性。

sentences.en: Or to translate.
sentences.zh: 或者换个通俗的说法来翻译。

sentences.en: It's basically like, don't just put a bird on it.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，别直接把一只鸟印上去完事。

sentences.en: Flowery designs don't necessarily look good.
sentences.zh: 繁复的花卉设计并不一定好看。

sentences.en: According to Jones, the best kinds of designs imply nature, while keeping with Proposition 8.
sentences.zh: 在琼斯看来，最好的设计既暗示自然，又符合第八条命题。

sentences.en: All ornaments should be based upon a geometrical construction.
sentences.zh: 所有装饰都应建立在几何结构的基础之上。

sentences.en: The quatrefoil is both geometrical and natural, but without being too flowery.
sentences.zh: 四叶形既具几何美感又源于自然，同时又不会显得过分繁复。

sentences.en: And this just might be what attracts designers to it over and over again,
sentences.zh: 这或许正是它一次又一次吸引设计师的原因，

sentences.en: and keeps it forever floating around us in iconographical drift.
sentences.zh: 并让它在图像学的漂移中永远环绕在我们身边。

sentences.en: My boys were born in a quatrefoil-shaped building in Chicago, the Prentiss Women's Hospital at Northwestern.
sentences.zh: 我的两个男孩出生在芝加哥的一栋四叶形建筑里，那是西北大学的普伦蒂斯妇女医院。

sentences.en: The whole building is in the shape of a quatrefoil, as seen from above.
sentences.zh: 从上方俯瞰，整栋建筑呈四叶形的形状。

sentences.en: It was cool looking, but according to the people at Northwestern,
sentences.zh: 它看起来很酷，但据西北大学的人说，

sentences.en: it was a pretty impractical shape for a modern research hospital.
sentences.zh: 对于现代研究型医院来说，这是一个相当不切实际的形状。

sentences.en: So it's been demolished.
sentences.zh: 所以它已经被拆除了。

sentences.en: A lot of people, including myself, were sad to see it go.
sentences.zh: 许多人，包括我自己，都为它的离去感到难过。

sentences.en: A Save Prentiss group tried to get the building landmark status.
sentences.zh: 一个名为“拯救普伦蒂斯”的组织曾试图为该建筑争取地标建筑地位。

sentences.en: Petitions were circulated, but the effort ultimately failed.
sentences.zh: 各方传阅了请愿书，但这一努力最终还是失败了。

sentences.en: But I think it's safe to say that no one would have cared at all
sentences.zh: 不过我认为可以肯定的是，如果没有人会在意，

sentences.en: if the building was not shaped like a quatrefoil.
sentences.zh: 如果这座建筑不是四叶形的。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffleman
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由埃弗里·特拉夫特曼制作，

sentences.en: with Katie Mingle, Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 合作者包括凯蒂·明格、萨姆·格林斯潘以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio, KALW in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 地方公共广播电台 KALW 的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 制作地点位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽市中心的杰出建筑事务所

sentences.en: a brilliant architecture firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: ArcSign 的办公室里。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并点赞本节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都开通了 Twitter、Instagram 和 Spotify。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links,
sentences.zh: 但要想了解关于这个故事的更多信息，包括精美的图片和链接，

sentences.en: and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible, you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 并收听《99%隐形》的所有单集，你必须访问 99pi.org。
